note: No request was given for this dispatch; the spec's own Summary was treated as the request, per the agent instructions.

findings.claim: REQ-03-019's absolute refusal rule and the contracts' Routes table description of the request-topics route give two different answers for a client principal calling GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/request-topics.

witness.detail: specs/requests/03-client-participants.md:192-196 (REQ-03-019): 'IF a client principal calls an organization route other than the requests list, a request they are the addressee of, that request's answer, decline and message routes, and the create and grant routes, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL answer 404.' The request-topics route is not in that named list. specs/requests/03-client-participants.contracts.md:62-67: 'The topics route is listed because the new-request modal reads it once per addressee kind and a case asserts what it returns for audience=client; it needs no capability — every active member reads the catalogue to fill the picker — and this spec does not amend it.' Read together with the Routes table row (contracts.md:44), the topics route's guard chain stays 'session, org scope' with no principal-kind check. apps/api/src/auth/session.guard.ts:15-32 confirms SessionGuard only re-reads the security stamp and never inspects principal kind, and OrgScopeGuard (referenced at contracts.md:28-29) only compares session.organizationId to the path orgId — which a client principal's session satisfies per REQ-03-003. So a client principal calling this route today, unamended, is answered 200, not the 404 REQ-03-019 requires of every route it does not name as an exception.

findings.suggestedFix: Either add the request-topics route to REQ-03-019's named exceptions (and state what it must answer a client — the existing catalogue, or a scoped subset) and drop the sentence saying the route is unamended; or state explicitly in the contracts that this route gains a principal-kind check that answers a client principal 404, replacing 'this spec does not amend it.' One answer, stated in both places.
